ADJOURNMENT
The next Compliance & Quality Committee meeting is scheduled on Monday, August 21, 2025, at 2:00 PM and may be conducted as a teleconference meeting.

Meeting Minutes – June 16, 2025
L.A. Care Health Plan CR 100, 1055 W. Seventh Street, Los Angeles, CA 90017
Members: Stephanie Booth, MD, Chairperson; Al Ballesteros, MBA; G. Michael Roybal, MD; Fatima Vazquez.
Senior Management: Terry Brown, Chief of Human Resources; Todd Gower, Chief Compliance Officer; Augustavia J. Haydel, General Counsel; Alex Li, Chief Health Equity Officer; Noah Paley, Chief of Staff; Edward Sheen, MD, Chief Quality and Population Health Executive.

CHAIRPERSON REPORT
Chairperson Booth suggested that members think about possible educational opportunities for the group. She state that with the new executive summaries being implemented, there were still mistakes, which she wanted to offer suggestions for improvement. She clarified the project belonged to the CEO and that questions could be directed to Martha Santana-Chin, Chief Executive Officer.
Chairperson Booth noted her goal was to make reports as valuable as possible. She noted that acronyms were still being used without explanation and that 'next steps' should clearly state planned follow-up actions. SheBelieved transparency was important. She also noted interest in comparing incentivized measures with performance changes to understand what was working and what was not. Todd Gower was working on a checklist to clarify risk types.

CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER REPORT
Mr. Gower reported updates on the Compliance Department’s activities and developments from DHCS, CMS, and DMHC. L.A. Care continues to face scrutiny regarding grievance timeliness, fraud waste and abuse awareness, and delegation oversight. Major priorities include implementing the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) system and expanding the fraud waste and abuse prevention program.

CHIEF MEDICAL OFFICER REPORT
Edward Sheen, MD provided updates. Sanctions for Medi-Cal in measurement year 2024 are projected to be much lower compared to 2023 and 2022—an estimated greater than 94% reduction. The estimated sanctions for 2024 are about $49,300, compared to $890,000 in 2022 and $214,000 in 2023. L.A. Care currently has an overall 3-star rating, but its Part C rating is 2.5 stars, which must reach 3 stars to remain viable. CAHPS scores are currently a challenge at around 1.8–1.9 stars.

QUALITY INCENTIVES: PAY-FOR-PERFORMANCE (P4P) UPDATES
Henock Solomon provided an update on L.A. Care’s P4P programs. These programs have been in place since 2010. High performers can earn $3–$4 PMPM, representing roughly 10–20% of bonus above capitation.

2025 CLINICAL INITIATIVES AND HEALTH EQUITY
Marina Acosta and Brigitte Bailey gave a report on reducing health disparities in HEDIS measures across Medi-Cal, L.A. Care Covered, and Medicare Plus. One project focuses on Black/African American children in South L.A. (SPA 6).

CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER REPORT OUT & AGENDA
Strategic Priorities: Advanced Compliance Technology Integration, Delegation Oversight Stabilization, Modernizing Compliance Reporting Tools, Cultivating a Culture of Compliance, Enhanced Regulatory Change Management.

INTERNAL AUDIT - ENFORCEMENT MATTER UPDATE
Gennadiy Daych, Director of Internal Audit, reported on activities related to 23 external audit findings. Top findings in 2024: Oversight Monitoring by Business Units (15), Lack of Policy and Procedure Adherence (14), and Regulatory Compliance (6).

CLAIMS INTEGRITY
Erik Chase reported on claims processing standards. 95% of claims must be processed within 30 calendar days. Beginning January 01, 2026, the Plan is required to process all claims within 30 calendar days per AB 3275. L.A. Care is monitoring suspicious hospice billing patterns.

APPEALS & GRIEVANCES
Demetra Crandall reported that Appeals volume increased by 17% (Jan-Jun 2025 vs Jan-Jun 2024). Grievance volume increased by 34%. Access to Primary Care Physician Office was the leading cause of access grievances at 32%.
